title: Customer token-spend SLO enforcement and region-failover telemetry
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Provide per-customer token-budget enforcement (soft and hard budgets), real-time telemetry to surface budget burn-rate against SLOs, and tie budget breaches to automated region-failover/circuit behaviour. This ticket covers the instrumentation schema, ingestion pipeline, alerting rules, and dashboard buildouts needed to make budget-driven failover predictable and debuggable.

Background: Customers have requested finer controls over their spend and stronger SLAs that can trigger graceful failover when their reserved capacity or spend budgets are exhausted. We currently have token-level latency SLIs and regional admission metrics, but lack a unified view that correlates customer budget burn, per-request token latency, KV-cache miss amplification, and the circuit state progression that leads to regional failovers.

Scope:
- Define a compact telemetry envelope for per-request budget attribution (customer_id, route, tokens_charged, kv_cache_hit, admitted_shard, latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, circuit_state). This must be low-overhead and streamable into our golden-signals ingestion pipeline.
- Implement a sampling mode for full token traces (1-5% by default) for tail-latency RCA without storing every tokenized event.
- Build a Grafana/Console dashboard for Customer Budget View: live burn-rate, projected exhaustion time, correlated p95/p99 token latency, kv-miss amplification, and active circuit states per region.
- Wire automation hooks: on soft budget breach, escalate to warning and switch customer traffic to cheaper model variant; on hard breach, trigger regional failover or routing to Dedicated fallback if configured. Automation will be governed by safe-rollout rules (cooldowns, hysteresis).

Non-goals: per-token replay storage, billing enforcement (billing will be a separate flow).
tasks: Design telemetry envelope and field-level cardinality limits
Add instrumentation to admission layer to emit budget attribution fields
Extend golden-signals ingestion to accept new envelope and tag joins
Implement 1% sampled token-trace export and storage TTL 14 days
Build Grafana + Console widgets for Customer Budget View and Budget Burn Timeline
Create alerting rules and escalation playbook (PagerDuty + Slack ops channel)
Safety review and rollout plan (canary on staging -> prod small customers)
Update runbooks and on-call checklist with failover validation steps
decisions: Store full sampled token traces for 14 days (tradeoff: actionable RCA vs storage cost)
Use p99 token latency as the primary SLI for budget-triggered failover; p95 shown as secondary
Sampling default = 1% across all customers; can opt-in to 5% for high-impact customers
Budget envelope will keep cardinality low: customer_id, route, short model fingerprint, region, shard_id
Soft budget breach = 5% of budget remaining projected within 10 minutes; Hard breach = budget exhausted
Automation cooldown = 2 minutes between automated routing changes for a given customer to avoid oscillation
updates: 2025-02-17: Kickoff meeting with Observability, Serving, and Console teams. Agreed on high-level envelope fields and storage TTL. Action: Aisha to draft Confluence spec.

2025-02-20: Prototype ingestion schema pushed to branch feat/customer-budget-schema (GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1287). Initial feedback from infra: ensure schema is JSON-lines friendly and avoids high-cardinality strings.
2025-02-24: Implemented instrumentation stub in admission-proxy; emits budget_attrib events (sampling off). Measured overhead: ~0.7% median CPU increase on admission path in local perf test.
2025-02-27: Iterated on sampling module; set default 1% and added per-customer override via tenant config (console flag). Added unit tests for sampling determinism.
2025-03-02: First draft dashboard templates uploaded to Grafana staging (dashboard id draft-231). Console team evaluating widget mapping to UI quotas.

2025-03-04: Safety review sync: confirmed automation hooks will require an explicit opt-in per-customer for hard failover. PM requested more conservative soft-breach thresholds; have action to test with synthetic workloads next week.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry envelope accepted by golden-signals ingestion without >0.1% EPS delta in pipeline backpressure tests
Dashboard shows per-customer burn-rate and projects exhaustion time within 2% accuracy for synthetic traffic patterns
Automated soft-breach action triggers in staging and routes customer to cheaper model variant without service interruption
Safety net prevents hard failover automation unless customer config opt-in is set
Runbook updated and on-call engineers can follow steps to validate a triggered failover end-to-end
notes_for_oncall: If you see sudden spikes in budget_burn_rate for multiple customers in a region, check for KV-cache regression (tag kv_cache_hit=false) first
Automated routing actions emit audit event audit:budget_action (search in logs) — use this to correlate with dashboard state
If ingestion pipeline lags, toggle sampling to 0.1% via feature-flag to reduce EPS until backfill completes
